name: Persians
place: Pars, the highlands of south-western Iran
desc: Herders of Pars who, under Cyrus, built the largest empire yet seen, governed it with roads, couriers and many tongues, let conquered peoples keep their gods, and laid out walled gardens they called paradise.
source: The Cyrus Cylinder (British Museum); the Bisotun inscription of Darius; the Persepolis Fortification Tablets; Herodotus

cautious: followed the underground channel by lamplight for a whole day
belligerent: took the place of a fallen man in the ranks so the ten thousand stayed ten thousand
gluttonous: rode the king's message from station to station without stopping

inventions.name: Qanat
inventions.source: Gently sloping tunnels that bring groundwater from the foot of the hills to the fields; spread across the empire under the Achaemenids
inventions.desc: A tunnel dug from the hills under the dry plain, so water flows to the fields without evaporating: farm plots yield 25% more.
inventions.hint: Needs Polished Stone Tools and farming, and builders who dig.

inventions.name: The Royal Road
inventions.source: Herodotus 8.98: 'Neither snow nor rain nor heat nor gloom of night' stops the Persian couriers riding from station to station
inventions.desc: A road with a fresh horse waiting at every station: everyone travels 8% faster and sees farther.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication and the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: Walled Paradise Garden
inventions.source: Old Persian pairidaeza, 'walled enclosure', gave Greek paradeisos and our word paradise; Cyrus' garden at Pasargadae had stone water channels
inventions.desc: Fruit trees and flowing water inside a wall, in four quarters: +4 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs farming, and builders who garden.

inventions.name: Ration Tablets
inventions.source: The Persepolis Fortification Tablets (c. 509–493 BCE) record rations for thousands of workers, with extra for women who had just given birth
inventions.desc: Every worker's share of grain, wine and beer written down, with more for new mothers: hunger grows 5% slower, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and someone to lead.

foods.name: The King's Table
foods.source: Polyaenus preserved a list of what was supplied for the Persian king's dinner each day: flour, birds, sheep, dates, raisins, pickled capers
foods.desc: Lamb, fowl, dates and raisins shared out to everyone in the household: +3 mood, hunger grows 5% slower.

foods.name: Almond and Raisin Rations
foods.desc: Nuts and dried fruit carried in a bag on the march: food spoils 10% slower.

finds.name: Wild Almonds
finds.desc: Trees that flower pink before any other, with nuts that must be chosen carefully: the bitter ones are poison.

finds.name: Wild Rhubarb
finds.desc: A mountain plant whose root purges sickness. The old stories say the first man and woman grew from one.

people.name: Bagapana
people.desc: He can find water under a dry hill by the plants that grow on it.
memory: dug a well-shaft forty men deep and struck water

people.name: Radushnamuya
people.desc: She writes down every worker's ration and never forgets a name.
memory: fed six hundred workers through a winter without one going hungry

people.name: Irdabama
people.desc: A noblewoman who ran her own estates and workshops with hundreds of workers, sealing orders with her own seal.

people.name: Achaemenes
people.source: Named by Darius at Bisotun as the founder of his line
people.desc: The forefather of the royal clan, of whom nothing is known but his name, which the kings repeated with pride.

people.name: Scylax
people.source: Herodotus 4.44: Darius sent Scylax down the Indus to the sea and around Arabia to Egypt
people.text: a Greek sea captain who has sailed down a great river of the east and around the deserts of Arabia.
memory: sailed thirty months from the mouth of the Indus to Egypt
people.desc: An explorer in the service of Darius.

people.name: Cyrus
people.label: Cyrus the Great
people.desc: A king who conquers and lets the conquered go home. Combat 7, Lore 6.

people.name: Darius
people.label: Darius the Organiser
people.desc: He gives the empire roads, coins and laws. Lore 7, Crafting 6.

people.name: Artemisia
people.label: Artemisia, Queen of the Ships
people.desc: A queen who commands her own ships in battle. Combat 7, Lore 4.

events.title: Let Them Go Home
events.source: The Cyrus Cylinder (539 BCE): Cyrus returned the gods of conquered cities to their shrines and let deported peoples go home
events.text: Among us live families taken long ago from a beaten clan, with the images of their gods. They work hard, but they still sing of home.

options.label: Let them go, gods and all

do.feat: Sent the captives home with their gods

options.result: They leave singing. Their clan sends gifts every year after, and calls our chief their shepherd.

options.label: They stay and work
options.result: The fields are well tended. The singing gets quieter.

events.title: Words on the Cliff
events.source: Darius carved his deeds at Bisotun, 100 m up a cliff, in Old Persian, Elamite and Babylonian; it became the key to reading cuneiform
events.text: The chief wants the tribe's story carved high on a cliff above the road, in every tongue that passes by, so that no one can ever say it was otherwise.

options.label: Carve it

do.feat: Carved the tribe's story on a cliff

options.result: Carvers hang on ropes for a whole summer. The cliff will speak for us long after we are gone.

options.label: Let the songs remember
options.result: The story stays in the mouths of the singers.

events.title: A Share for the Mothers
events.source: Persepolis tablets give women who had just given birth extra rations, more for a boy, but given to both
events.text: The steward proposes that every woman who has just borne a child get an extra share of grain and wine for a month.

tales.name: The First Two from the Rhubarb
tales.source: The Bundahishn, a Zoroastrian creation text written down in the 9th century CE from older tradition
tales.text: When the first man died, his seed fell to earth, and after forty years a rhubarb plant grew from it with two stems so close together that no one could tell them apart. The stems became a man and a woman, Mashya and Mashyana, the parents of all people.

tales.name: The Herdsman's Son
tales.text: A boy raised by a cowherd played king with the village children, and gave them orders like a real king. When a nobleman's son refused, the boy had him beaten. Brought before the king, he answered so proudly that the king recognised his own grandson, whom he had ordered left to die.

tales.name: The Horse That Chose a King
tales.text: Six nobles agreed that whoever's horse neighed first at sunrise would be king. Darius' groom let his master's stallion smell a mare at that very spot the night before. In the morning the stallion neighed, lightning flashed from a clear sky, and the others bowed.

tales.name: The New Day
tales.source: Nowruz, the Iranian new year at the spring equinox; later tradition ties it to the legendary king Jamshid
tales.text: When the day and the night are equal and spring begins, the people light fires, jump over them, wash, and wear new clothes. The legendary king Jamshid first sat on his jewelled throne on this day, and the sun shone on it so brightly that the people called it the New Day.
